sources.title: Gone With the Water: The Loss of Genetic Variability in Black and Gold Howler Monkeys (Alouatta caraya) Due to Dam Construction
sources.version: Frontiers in Ecology and Evolution 10:768652; version of record published 2022-03-10
sources.locator: Abstract; Materials and Methods, Study Sites Description and Sampling; Results; Discussion, Genetic Diversity Gone With the Water.
sources.scope: Primary population-genetics study of 256 individuals across 22 sites in Argentina, Paraguay, and Brazil, including four sites sampled before dam-linked flooding; microsatellite and mitochondrial markers. The authors explicitly state that sampling does not cover the entire species range.
sources.license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), stated in the article copyright and license section.
sources.licenseAppliesTo: Article text; separately credited third-party material is excluded.
sources.rightsEvidenceLocator: Copyright and license statement at article end.
sources.attribution: Oklander LI, Caputo M, Fernández GP, Jerusalinsky L, de Oliveira SF, Bonatto SL, and Corach D (2022). Gone With the Water: The Loss of Genetic Variability in Black and Gold Howler Monkeys (Alouatta caraya) Due to Dam Construction. Frontiers in Ecology and Evolution 10:768652. https://doi.org/10.3389/fevo.2022.768652. Claims are paraphrased.

claims.text: The study compared genetic structure across 22 sites. It evaluated microsatellite variability in 256 individuals and mitochondrial sequences in 112 individuals; four sites had been sampled before dam-linked flooding.
claims.scope: Study samples and markers only; not a complete census of the species range.

claims.text: Samples from four flooded sites had higher genetic variability than samples from remaining studied sites. Fourteen mitochondrial haplotypes were reported at flooded sites; thirteen were not detected at the remaining sampled sites.
claims.scope: The paper says these lineages may have been lost locally, but notes incomplete range coverage; no claim is made that they are absent from all other populations.

gaps: No multi-source species dossier is added.
Current range-wide distribution, population size, and conservation assessment are not addressed.
